gaps.sentence: ___ spaceship travelled for six months before reaching Mars.
gaps.explanation: The spaceship — the one in the story; Mars takes no article.

gaps.sentence: He wants to become ___ engineer when he grows up.
gaps.explanation: Professions take a/an; 'engineer' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: He is ___ honest man; everyone trusts him.
gaps.explanation: 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so 'an'.

gaps.sentence: My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

gaps.sentence: She arrived in ___ New York on Monday evening.
gaps.explanation: City names take no article: New York, London, Madrid.
Plural general nouns and flu (illness name) take no article.

gaps.sentence: I live on ___ Baker Street, near the tube station.
gaps.explanation: Street names take no article: Baker Street, Oxford Street.

gaps.sentence: ___ sales figures for October look promising.
gaps.explanation: 'The sales figures for October' — defined by the for-phrase.
